name: crew
description: The orchestrator/worker session model over herdr or Orca, the project file's declared layer. An orchestrator session keeps its context for decisions and dispatches everything else to worker sessions launched by seat name: the operator's own files name each seat (~/.claude/crew/agents.md on the machine, .crew/roles.md in the project), implementers route by complexity class, one reviewer session runs its review command (/code-review by default) once per PR, the retained implementer works GitHub threads to zero; the run merges on a clean gate set under its merge word (standing by default); an operator gate makes it wait for the operator's word. A session budget caps each work item at one implementer and one verifier. Each seat gets its own labelled tab holding one full-size pane, in the tree its --cwd names, so a run of five seats is five readable tabs. Readiness is derived, not declared: a seat herdr detects waits on a typed agent state, a seat it does not waits on a screen pattern, so an undetected agent CLI is a first-class seat and a detection manifest later upgrades it with no edit. A run's state lives in a dagr run.json the plugin's prose owns; Codex has no plugin bin/, so the check-then-rename write stays a hand loop there (the Claude Code and OMP surfaces ship bin/crew-run for it). One fail-open hook, on Claude Code only, tells a seat its own context figure past a ceiling of 500000 tokens — a coordinator seat rotates on it, a leaf finishes; where molt runs, a child hands off to its parent and the top molts in place. Defers every other layer command to that layer's own guide. No lib, no state.

interface.shortDescription: Orchestrator/worker session model over herdr or Orca.
interface.longDescription: Crew states who does what when one orchestrator session drives worker sessions through the project's layer (herdr or Orca, the project file's declared layer): which named seat fills each role, what a brief must carry, where the orchestrator stops and dispatches instead, one code review per PR with findings returned through the seat's report file, GitHub threads worked to zero. The run merges on a clean gate set under its merge word (standing by default); an operator gate makes it wait for the operator's word. It defers every other layer command to that layer's own version-matched guide.
